newsitem.title: FRANCE: French rate cut widely expected on Thursday - poll.
newsitem.headline: French rate cut widely expected on Thursday - poll.

text.p: A majority of economists polled by Reuters on Tuesday said they believe another official interest rate cut is likely when the Bank of France's monetary policy council meets on Thursday.

Fifteen of 20 economists polled forecast a decision to cut the key intervention rate -- currently at 3.25 percent -- by about 10 basis points. Failing that, the bank could offer a signal of continued easing by cutting the less important 5-to-10 day emergency lending rate, several said.

Those favouring a cut say the time is ripe, with the franc relatively steady at around 3.38 versus the mark, for the bank to narrow the gap between the intervention rate and the German repo rate, which currently stands at 3.00 percent.

Among the pro-cut majority, several said a symbolic cut of as much as 25 basis points in the 5-to-10 day rate was possible if the Bank held off on the more important intervention rate at which the French central bank allocates repo funds.
There is no securities repurchase tender on Thursday because of timing problems due to back-to-back holidays this weekend and next. November 1 and 11 are both public holidays.
But the monetary policy council will meet and a spokeswoman said: "If there is an announcement, it will be at the time we normally do it, around 1315 (1215 GMT)".

The intervention rate was last cut, from 3.35 percent, on September 19. The 5-to-10-day rate, which sets the ceiling for money market rates, was last cut to 4.75 percent from 4.90 percent on August 1.
